LanguageData.MG_Horse.label: Mengwu Horse
LanguageData.MG_Horse.description:
Carefully bred by the Mengwu people, this horse is faster, more intelligent and less wild than ordinary horses. Scarce grazing in its homeland also favoured a breed that needs to feed less often.

An indispensable companion to Mengwu nomads, it is also the preferred mount of their cavalry.

Mengwu horses are most common on grasslands, but also inhabit temperate and cold forests.

LanguageData.MG_TiaoShu.label: Mogul Leaping Bunny
LanguageData.MG_TiaoShu.description: Once endangered on old Shenzhou, this small leaping rodent thrived after being introduced to the rimworlds. Mengwu herders keep it as a pet, and its image appears on their totems.\n\nWild populations favour semi-desert habitats and need little food. They also occur in forests.

LanguageData.MG_TuSun.label: Rabbit mantle
LanguageData.MG_TuSun.description: A Pallas's cat native to cold regions of old Shenzhou. Adapted to harsh conditions and sparse food, it nevertheless came close to extinction there. A Mengwu wildlife conservation organisation introduced it to the rimworlds.\n\nIt still hunts small animals such as rodents. Since its introduction, it has become more resilient and more comfortable around people, making it better suited to life as a pet.

LanguageData.MG_TuBoShu.label: Mongolian Woody Groundhog
LanguageData.MG_TuBoShu.description: A burrowing rodent from the semi-arid grasslands of old Shenzhou, brought to the rimworlds by Mengwu biologists. It tolerates cold conditions and also thrives in areas with plentiful rainfall.\n\nSome Mengwu people keep these groundhogs as pets, while others hunt them for food.
